speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. Can you tell me if you have been experiencing headaches, blurry vision, or nosebleeds recently? Also, do you have any family history of high blood pressure or kidney disease?

speaker: Patient
text: 5-year-old boy. The patient is presented by his mother for a well-child visit. The boy was born at 39 weeks gestation via spontaneous vaginal delivery, is currently up to date on all vaccines, and is meeting all developmental milestones. His mother reports that he has been generally doing well with no concerns. No family history of cardiovascular disease. The boy does not take any medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: I see; at a well-child visit, we must be vigilant as hypertension can be asymptomatic. Has your son ever had his blood pressure measured before today, and if so, what were the results? Additionally, please describe his exact height and weight percentiles.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is High blood pressure on the right upper extremity.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Coarctation of the Aorta.

I have identified a discrepancy between the child's asymptomatic status and the reported isolated right upper extremity hypertension, which strongly suggests a structural defect. Please confirm if there are any differences in pulse strength or blood pressure when measured in his legs compared to his arms. REQUEST IMAGES: Echocardiogram, Abdominal Aorta Ultrasound.
